answer.location_description: A small patch below and right of the image centre, around rows 19-21 and columns 16-20. It is strongest at (20,18), (20,19) and (19,16), just outside the region where the blob usually sits.
answer.shortcut_type: localized bright spot/patch (small marker) in lower-right of blob area
answer.mechanism: The layer-1 units fall into two families. The small-blob family (0, 3, 5, 8, 14, 15, 18, 20, 23, 24, 25, 28, 31) has a positive centre, a negative annulus and a positive periphery. It feeds layer-2 unit u9 (weights roughly +58 to +94), and u9 has output weight -98, so this family pushes toward class 0. The large-blob family (1, 6, 9, 10, 12, 16, 27, 30) has a positive annulus. It feeds u4 (output weight +99) and is negative on u9, so it pushes toward class 1. At the patch the two families carry opposite-signed, unusually large weights: strongly positive in the small-blob units and strongly negative in the large-blob units. Brightness in this patch therefore raises the class-0 pathway and suppresses the class-1 pathway at the same time, pushing the output toward 'small blob' regardless of blob size.
answer.evidence:
Small-blob-family weights at the patch versus their usual periphery values of about 20-50:
- Row 20, columns 18-19: unit 0 65/81; unit 18 78 at column 19; unit 25 80 at column 19; unit 28 83 at column 19; unit 15 75/63; unit 20 73/54; unit 31 61/68; unit 5 65 at column 17.
- Row 19, column 16: unit 0 58, unit 3 64, unit 8 66, unit 15 70, unit 20 67, unit 23 84.
Large-blob-family weights at the same pixels versus a near-zero (±30) periphery:
- Row 20, column 19: unit 1 -69, unit 6 -65, unit 12 -46, unit 16 -49 (and -58 at column 18), unit 9 -39.
- Row 20, columns 17-19: unit 10 -53/-40/-29; unit 30 -48 at column 17.
- Row 19, column 16: unit 30 -56, unit 16 -54, unit 1 -51, unit 10 -48.
Row 21, columns 17-18 shows the opposite sign: negative in units 5, 25, 28 and 31, positive in units 30, 27 and 16. This gives a sharp local contrast that blob-size features would not produce. No comparable localized hotspot appears anywhere else in the periphery.
answer.main_feature: Centre-surround detectors on the blob: the large-blob family fires when the annulus around the centre (roughly rows 6-17, columns 6-17) is bright, and the small-blob family fires when that annulus is dark while the very centre is bright. A uniform-positive unit (19) also tracks overall brightness.
